claims.text: A controlled sub-Tg anneal immediately after rapid solidification will improve glass-forming ability.
A controlled sub-Tg anneal immediately after rapid solidification will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
Rapid solidification can produce an amorphous Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-P alloy.
Rapidly solidified phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys possess significant excess free volume.
Rapidly solidified phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys possess significant internal stresses.
A short anneal below Tg allows atomic relaxation without initiating crystallization.
Sub-Tg annealing enhances atomic relaxation in the amorphous phase.
Annealing-induced structural relaxation decreases free volume.
Annealing-induced structural relaxation decreases internal stresses.
Reducing free volume and internal stresses reduces the tendency for subsequent crystallization.
The sub-Tg anneal will increase the crystallization onset temperature relative to an as-quenched alloy.
The sub-Tg anneal will increase the critical casting diameter relative to an as-quenched alloy.
The beneficial effect occurs only when annealing is maintained strictly below Tg.
Annealing durations that permit crystallization negate the beneficial effect.
Significantly different cooling conditions may negate the beneficial effect.

contradictions.description: The intervention is applied only after rapid solidification, but the predicted glass-forming improvement is expressed as a higher critical casting diameter, a formation-stage metric. The experiment anneals already-solidified samples and does not specify a casting series or another protocol by which the post-solidification treatment could change or validly determine critical casting diameter.
